suggestions.text: At Cascade, developers spend about 30% of their time on models and the rest negotiating land leases, interconnection, and offtake contracts; developers own projects from site selection through financing, while asset managers take over once projects operate. This directly suggests a deal-making-heavy role, though the exact split may vary by developer or project.

Cascade developers are usually based in Denver or Boulder, but two work remotely from Durango, so a mountain-town location appears possible there, though it seems uncommon and the remote-work arrangement is not fully explained.
Cascade usually hires two MBA interns and decides by mid-January.
Priya offered to introduce you to Luis Ortega, who runs Cascade’s storage team.
Send Priya your resume this week and read up on the interconnection queue before your next conversation.
At Basecamp, project managers spend two or three days a week on site during the building season, so the role includes significant field work; how the week looks outside that season remains unknown.
Sam said Basecamp pay is lower than energy roles but includes profit sharing; the size of the pay gap and how profit sharing works remain unknown.
Basecamp has eleven people, and most of its revenue comes from towns and counties using public grants, making project timing dependent on grants.
Send Sam a one-page note describing how you would approach the grant pipeline for two projects.
Sam would consider a summer MBA fellow if the fellow could own grant applications for two projects.
